prompt.title: Notice your paradigm
prompt.text: Before you change what you do, look at how you see things. This exercise catches you in the act: three short steps, about 15 minutes.
prompt.whyItMatters: Two people can watch the same moment and tell two different stories. Each is sure they're just saying what happened. Once you've felt that gap, you can check your lens before changing a habit. The book calls that lens a paradigm.

step1.viewA: You wave to a coworker in the hallway. They walk straight past, eyes on their phone. You spend the rest of the day wondering what you did wrong.

firstView.prompt: Why do you think they didn't wave back?
firstView.label: Your first guess
firstView.placeholder: e.g. They're annoyed about yesterday's meeting and are avoiding me.

step1.revealHint: Write your guess first, then see the other side.
step1.viewB: Just before you waved, they got a message: their kid's school was calling. They were reading it and typing a reply as they walked. They never saw you.

switchDifficulty.prompt: How hard was it to drop your first guess?
switchDifficulty.label: Difficulty

step2.intro: Think of three things you've tried to change about yourself. Some were quick fixes: a trick, a tool, a new rule. Some went deeper: you became a bit different. The book calls the first kind technique and the second character.

attempt.prompt: What did you try to change?
attempt.label: What you tried
attempt.placeholder3: e.g. Put money aside every month

kind.prompt: Was it a quick fix or a real change?

difference.prompt: What's the real difference between a quick fix and a real change? One sentence.
difference.label: The difference
difference.placeholder: e.g. A quick fix works while I'm watching it. A real change keeps working when I'm not.

step3.intro: How you see a situation shapes what you do. What you do shapes what you get. Pick one situation that's bothering you. Trace it twice: as you see it now, and through a different lens.

do.placeholder: e.g. I nag and check their homework every night

get.placeholder: e.g. Arguments, and they do even less

see.placeholder: e.g. My teenager is overwhelmed and doesn't know where to start

do.placeholder: e.g. I ask what's hard and help them plan the first step

get.placeholder: e.g. Quieter evenings and a bit more done each day

checklist.firstView: Write why you think they didn't wave back
checklist.difficulty: Rate how hard it was to drop your first guess

guide.inShort: You'll read a short scene and guess what happened, then see the other side. Then you'll sort three of your own change attempts into quick fixes and real changes. Last, you'll trace one situation through two lenses. About 15 minutes. You'll end with one situation you can look at differently this week.
howTo: Read the hallway scene and write your first guess about why they didn't wave back.
Tap "Show why", then rate how hard it was to let go of your guess.
Write three things you've tried to change about yourself. Mark each one a quick fix or a real change.
In one sentence, say what the difference is between the two.
Pick a situation that's bothering you. Write what you see, what you do, and what you get.
Write the same situation through a different lens: what you'd see, do, and get.
Mark done when all three steps are filled in. You can come back and edit any time.

guide.afterwards: This week, catch one moment when your first guess about someone turns out wrong. Come back and add it to your notes. Then go on to the next exercise on the list.
